sections.title: Executive diagnosis
sections.purpose: Start with what MK concluded: the position, the pattern beneath it, the strengths, the exposure themes and the leadership priorities. By the end of this section an executive understands the full management story.
sections.takeaway: The whole management story in three pages.

sections.title: Scope and analytical basis
sections.purpose: One concise page: the self-assessment basis and the boundary, strategic analysis and control design, not independent verification.
sections.takeaway: What the report can and cannot say.

sections.title: Readiness profile
sections.purpose: The ten areas, interpreted: the shape of the environment, not a list of figures.
sections.takeaway: Where the environment holds and where it is open.

sections.title: Systemic themes
sections.purpose: The cross-cutting themes and how they interact: which weakness provides opportunity and which delays detection or response.
sections.takeaway: Why the themes must be treated together.

sections.title: Findings
sections.purpose: Deeper advisory findings: the recorded condition, the control-system context, interaction with other controls, the plausible pathway, the management consequence and why the target design matters.
sections.takeaway: What each weakness means in this organisation.

sections.title: Fraud exposure and pathways
sections.purpose: Organisation-relevant fraud pathways and the exposure themes they demonstrate.
sections.takeaway: How the weaknesses combine into loss.

sections.title: Target fraud-control environment
sections.purpose: The priority control blueprints: current state, target state, how each should operate, what it connects to and how effectiveness is measured, in prose with a compact specification panel.

sections.title: Target fraud-risk operating model
sections.purpose: Who owns fraud risk, who operates the controls, who monitors, who investigates, who escalates and who oversees, proportionate to the organisation.

sections.title: Leadership decisions
sections.purpose: The real decisions executives must take, explaining the approved options, trade-offs and MK's recommended route without adding options.
sections.takeaway: The choices only leadership can make.

sections.title: Twelve-month implementation blueprint
sections.purpose: Stabilise, Establish, Embed and Mature as proposed stages: outcomes, owners and dependencies, not walls of control text, and not deadlines.
sections.takeaway: How the organisation gets from here to there.

sections.title: Management fraud-readiness scorecard
sections.purpose: Practical measures with owners, frequency and escalation thresholds.
sections.takeaway: How management will know it is working.

sections.title: Methodology and limitations
sections.purpose: Concise product boundary and how the position is read, including what awaits MK's approval.

sections.title: Management conclusion
sections.purpose: Where the organisation is, the transition required, the foundations that matter most, what success looks like by ninety days and by twelve months, and when Advisory would add value.
